stories.headline: Avalanche's Logan O'Connor, Zachary L'Heureux may return on trip
stories.summary: Banged-up Colorado forwards Logan O'Connor and Zachary L'Heureux could make their season debuts this week during a two-game road swing.
stories.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Banged-up Colorado forwards Logan O'Connor and Zachary L'Heureux could make their season debuts this week during a two-game road swing.

It's more offense for an Avalanche team that's started the season 2-0 and has scored 14 goals. O'Connor and L'Heureux have been sidelined with lower-body injuries. Avalanche coach Jared Bednar said Tuesday after practice he expects them to play either Wednesday night in Winnipeg or Thursday night at Calgary -- maybe even both.

L'Heureux was acquired along with center Fedor Svechkov in June as part of a deal that sent forward Jack Drury to Nashville.

"You always want to be healthy for Game 1 and I'm on the shelf, so it's not fun," L'Heureux said after being a full participant in practice Tuesday. "But I'm lucky and fortunate that it's not something major and I was able to rehab it quick enough. I'm ready to go now."

A first-round pick by the Predators in 2021, L'Heureux has played in 87 career NHL games, with nine goals and 11 assists. He also has 84 penalty minutes. L'Heureux drew a suspension during the 2024-25 season for slew-footing Minnesota defenseman Jared Spurgeon.

Bednar compared L'Heureux playing on the edge to a younger version of Nazem Kadri.

"He's matured into knowing when he has to play physical and play with grit, and when he can tone that down a little bit," Bednar said of the 36-year-old Kadri. "He's not as reactive as he was when he was a young guy.

"We'll just watch (L'Heureux) play and have discussions on when we think he needs to dial it back a little bit or when he needs to ramp it up a little bit. But I don't like to prejudge guys. It's a different culture. It's a different locker room. It's a different team. He's maturing, daily, and we'll see where he gets to in this game."

O'Connor missed the opening 69 games last season after undergoing hip surgery. He dressed in all 13 playoff games as the Avalanche made it to the Western Conference Final before being swept by Vegas.

stories.headline: Did you miss the NBA offseason? Here's what to know for fantasy basketball
stories.summary: Jim McCormick highlights all the changes -- and other things to know -- heading into the new fantasy basketball season.
stories.body:
Maybe your fantasy football team has started the season like the Los Angeles Chargers. In fact, maybe your fantasy football team is full of Los Angeles Chargers. Either way, welcome to another season of fantasy hoops.

Whether making an annual gridiron-to-hardwood pivot or coming to our game for the first time, you need not track every Shams Charania post or dissect every roster to get up to speed. We have you covered.

Some blend of the second apron -- think Jaylen Brown -- and second destinations -- Ja Morant and LaMelo Ball -- drove many of this summer's biggest moves. The goal is to decipher meaningful changes in the fantasy basketball landscape after a busy, dramatic offseason.

The All-Star Carousel
You know the big names who changed teams, but who is set to surge or sacrifice statistically? With apologies to Khris Middleton and D'Angelo Russell, we'll conduct a stock report on the following former All-Stars who changed teams this offseason. To get a sense of how the market values them, they are listed in order of ESPN average draft position.

Familiar First-rounder: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Miami Heat
A lost final season in Milwaukee gives way to a featured role in a coaching culture that gets the most out of elite, versatile forwards. Will the Heat lead the league in pace again now that this pick-and-roll engine is rostered? If the tempo remains, could this be his best statistical season in years? Consider me, along with Pat Riley, a believer

Health Permitting: LaMelo Ball, Minnesota Timberwolves and Kawhi Leonard, Toronto Raptors
Ball will almost certainly average more than the modest 28 minutes per game he hovered around in Charlotte last year. The front office consolidated the rotation, putting this big, brilliant playmaker on track for 30-plus minutes per night. Charlotte's breakneck, shoot-first system was ideal for his skill set, leaving a real question of offensive fit. Fit and health make Ball a risky, potentially rewarding pick.

Leonard is also in a better position to produce in Toronto; Scottie Barnes can take the toughest, most physical defensive assignments while providing playmaking gravity. Leonard is a league-winner if he plays more than 65 games.

Which Philly Forward? Jaylen Brown and LeBron James
This one is simple: Brown's potential to repeat last season's epic, MVP-caliber campaign is, well, quite low. Even with the market pricing in an expected sacrifice, it's hard to envision Brown providing a fantasy profit. Despite my Philly fandom, it's sensible to fade Brown.

James, on the other hand, could outperform his draft spot in a table-setting role rich in potential-and realized-assists. With pocket passes to Joel Embiid and slashes from Brown, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, can James recapture, or at least approach, the playmaking form that carried him to the passing title as the point guard of the 2019-20 Lakers?

Not that it has hurt his fantasy price, but I believe the tradeoff in touches or usage that Maxey makes for efficiency will prove profitable. I'm drafting him confidently at his draft price. Embiid? Re-read the Leonard blurb.

Get Buckets: Julius Randle, Brooklyn Nets and Tyler Herro, Milwaukee Bucks
These two remind me of a classic Eddie House scouting report: "Won't shoot unless he has the ball in his hands." Randle's usage in the post could mirror his best numbers from his days across the bridge in Manhattan. It's unlikely, however, that Randle will sustain the volume of minutes and touches from his prime, especially on a team incentivized to develop talent. That said, Randle is going to put up really fun tallies in points leagues when he's running hot.

No longer riding shotgun in South Beach, Herro can finally be, well, a hero. The Bucks have some incumbent guard talent in Ryan Rollins and Kevin Porter Jr., but no real competition for Herro's touches. The Wisconsin native will run a gauntlet of screens and command pick-and-roll duties in Taylor Jenkins' system. Found late in the middle rounds, Herro has the ingredients for big numbers.

Ripple Effects
When stars change teams, so do multiple rosters and rotations. While we focus on the stars, sometimes it's the secondary shifts that create the most value. Consider this the ripple effect of such seismic transactions.

A massive move such as Ball to the Timberwolves fittingly earns attention. Coby White? Not as much. This confident, heat-check artist should soak up minutes, playmaking touches, and gobs of shooting possessions as an important lead guard in Charlotte. I've already deemed Brandon Miller a breakout candidate given the usage and shots Ball vacates.

Sadly, Ja Morant is no longer inherently in the high-impact club above. There is still, of course, reason to track Morant's preseason play and eye test, as this is a former game-changing talent. The glut of guards in Portland curbs enthusiasm, especially given how odd the fit with Damian Lillard -- and even Scoot Henderson -- seems. Be dubious about a revival in this second destination.

A potentially positive ripple from the Morant move is Ty Jerome. This fun, if fragile, combo guard has posted absurd scoring and shooting splits whenever active in recent seasons. With Morant's ball-dominant game now out west, Jerome is an ideal ripple player to target.

Lost in the wake of Antetokounmpo's move to Miami is that Norman Powell is set to consume even more minutes, touches, and freedom to find his own shot in Chicago. I'm finding Powell on my rosters more often this fall. With the Detroit Pistons somewhat oddly purging their frontcourt, John Collins could be a massive winner from a statistical standpoint and a somewhat rogue winner of the offseason.

Dusty May, Micah Nori, and Sean Sweeney are all taking their first NBA head-coaching jobs, while Tiago Splitter gets his first full-time gig, adding another layer of uncertainty-and opportunity-to several already reshaped rosters. Keep an eye out for team-wide preseason trends such as pace and offensive rebounding rates, as these are some of the stickiest stats from preseason to the regular season and could provide early tells for these new clipboards.

Trendspotting

It helps to consider the larger, league-wide trends influencing the fantasy market. For instance, with so many proven offensive engines -- Luka Doncic, Cade Cunningham, Nikola Jokic, James Harden, Giannis -- and, conversely, so many modern share-the-ball systems, teams are less likely to funnel their offenses through mediocre playmakers.

Fewer offenses are built around one player creating everything; more have several four-to-six-assist players instead of a single 10-assist engine. That makes the remaining elite initiators more structurally valuable, while a superficially "good" five-assist guard may be easier to replace than old draft habits suggest.

This does also put a premium on players with predicted playmaking upside; Ajay Mitchell, Jerome, White, Darius Acuff Jr., Egor Demin, and Davion Mitchell come to mind. The scarcity of bankable creation also makes me more likely to take on risks in potentially elite passers like Darius Garland and even Lillard. Set reminder: chase creation.

Size matters, too. While lead playmakers are still the coin of the realm, size-particularly effectiveness on the glass and in rim protection-is being prioritized with each new French Alien. Or just the one. While only one fantasy team, just like in the NBA, can roster Victor Wembanyama, the wingspan race to keep up has surfaced in fantasy as well. You'll want to prioritize size and effectiveness in rebounding and blocks, no longer as an afterthought that can be made up with rim runners and waiver wonders.

Heading into your draft, remember that not every jersey swap is positive-and not every one is negative. The value lies in the context: role, teammates, pace, touches, and the opportunity left behind. Coaching changes will take time to reveal themselves, but attentive managers can read early signals before the market catches up.

More broadly, the ripples and trends are where value lives in a season defined by movement. Treat every major transaction as a prompt to look beyond the player in the headline; finding the other side of the move is a winning habit to carry into your draft.

stories.headline: Fred Claire, ex-Dodgers GM who oversaw 1988 WS team, dies at 91
stories.summary: Fred Claire, who parlayed early jobs as a sportswriter and editor into a 30-year career with the Dodgers in public relations and as a World Series-winning GM, has died. He was 91.
stories.body:
PASADENA, Calif. -- Fred Claire, who parlayed early jobs as a sportswriter and editor into a 30-year career with the Los Angeles Dodgers in public relations and as a World Series-winning general manager, has died. He was 91.

Claire died Monday, on his 91st birthday, in Pasadena, the team announced Tuesday. Claire had entered hospice care recently.

In January 2015, at age 80, Claire was diagnosed with squamous cell skin cancer on his lip. He had the cells removed, but the cancer later returned in his jaw and again in his neck. He had surgery to remove a nerve on the left side of his face along with several lymph nodes. He underwent radiation, chemotherapy and immunotherapy as part of his 11-year journey with cancer.

He would jog regularly during his years on the road as the general manager and said he was diligent about wearing sunscreen except on his lips.

"Fred brought many victories and Dodger legends to our franchise, as well as the 1988 World Series title," team president and CEO Stan Kasten said in a statement, "and we are forever grateful for his leadership during such a memorable era."

Claire was covering the Dodgers during spring training in Florida for the Long Beach Press-Telegram in 1969 when one of the team's public relations assistants was fired.

He expressed interest in the job and was hired that July. He was promoted to vice president of public relations and promotions in 1975.

During his tenure, Claire was instrumental in creating the Dodger Blue branding and Think Blue campaign. The club drew 3.3 million fans in 1978, the first MLB team to exceed 3 million. He also hired announcer Ross Porter, who worked for the team from 1977 until being let go in 2004.

In 1976, Chicago Cubs outfielder Rick Monday ran over and saved an American flag from being burned on the Dodger Stadium field by two spectators. Claire directed the message board operator to type the words: "Rick Monday......You Made a Great Play" on the board.

In April 1987, a public relations firestorm occurred over comments 70-year-old general manager Al Campanis made on ABC's "Nightline."

Campanis, who was white, was asked by host Ted Koppel about the lack of Black people in significant positions of authority in baseball.

"I truly believe they may not have some of the necessities to be, let's say, a field manager, or perhaps, a general manager," Campanis said. "Why are Black people not good swimmers? Because they don't have buoyancy."

Campanis had agreed to the interview without telling anyone in the Dodgers organization. Claire awoke the next day to a story about Campanis' comments in the newspaper.

"I couldn't believe what I was reading," he wrote in his 2004 memoir.

Campanis had been Jackie Robinson's roommate when the two were in the minor leagues in 1946, and he tutored Robinson in transitioning from shortstop to second base. Robinson broke baseball's color barrier with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947.

"Those who knew Al expressed shock. There had never been a hint of bigotry in anything he had ever said or done," Claire wrote. "In my view, what Al had attempted to do that night was to defend his beloved game of baseball in an area where there was no defense."

Campanis was fired after two decades as GM. Team owner Peter O'Malley handed control of one of the most storied teams in baseball to Claire. He accepted on the condition that he would have total and complete responsibility for baseball operations.

Claire wasn't intimidated, either, having been involved in discussions regarding free agents, arbitration and team payroll since becoming a team vice president in 1975.

In Claire's first full season as GM in 1987, the Dodgers finished with a 73-89. O'Malley informed Claire he was considering bringing in a more experienced person for the job. He called the New York Mets and asked for permission to speak to Joe McIlvaine, but was denied. O'Malley decided to stick with Claire.

"Fred was a talented team player and everyone in the organization enjoyed working with him," O'Malley said in a statement.

He is survived by wife, Sheryl, and children Jeff, Jennifer and Kim.

Atlético Madrid and Juventus are monitoring Arsenal winger Noni Madueke with a view to a loan move, while SC Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic has Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea on his trail. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

stories.headline: What's next: Will Silva's first title defense be against Shevchenko?
stories.summary: The most likely opponent and a wild card for the winners and losers on the UFC 332 main card.
stories.body:
The UFC has a new women's flyweight champion for the first time in over two years following the UFC 332 main event in Salt Lake City on Saturday night. And with a new champion comes brand-new matchups. After winning the belt via unanimous decision over Wang Cong, Natalia Silva will have no shortage of challengers looking for their shot at gold.

Also on the UFC 332 fight card, rising men's bantamweight contender Payton Talbott made quick work of former two-time men's flyweight champion Deiveson Figueiredo in the co-main event. Talbott could take on a top-ranked contender in his next Octagon appearance. And a handful of young prospects earned impressive first-round knockout victories.

Here's what's next for the top stars of UFC 332.

Natalia Silva, women's flyweight champion

Who should be next: Valentina Shevchenko

The state of the UFC's women's divisions is not ideal. We haven't seen a bantamweight title fight all year, due to injuries to Kayla Harrison. Mackenzie Dern is the strawweight champion, but (fair or not) there is a pretty significant need for her to fight Zhang Weili to validate her standing as the top 115-pound fighter in the world, since Zhang vacated her belt, never lost it in competition. Now the same is true of the flyweight title. Silva has the longest active win streak at 125 pounds and might be the best in the world, but she'll battle for that perception until she fights Shevchenko. We'll have to see how long Shevchenko is out, but this fight needs to happen as soon as possible.

Wild card: Erin Blanchfield

Blanchfield has looked like future champion material since she debuted with the UFC at 22 years old in 2021. She's now five years into her UFC career, and she is 8-1 with one learning experience in the form of a five-round decision loss to Manon Fiorot in 2024. She's still only 27 and could well prove to be the future of this weight class. She's got a tough matchup scheduled against Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17. If she gets past that unscathed, the UFC could easily book her with Silva as soon as possible, instead of waiting for Shevchenko.

Payton Talbott, men's bantamweight
Who should be next: Sean O'Malley

It has to be done. O'Malley was once the darling of the bantamweight division. Now it's Talbott, and it's hard to deny this matchup. Now, the UFC is almost certainly already looking at O'Malley for an upcoming title fight. Especially if Petr Yan defeats Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333 later this month, O'Malley is the favorite to face Yan next. But if UFC fans were polled, the more anticipated fight might honestly be O'Malley vs. Talbott. Not to get out of control here, but this could headline a numbered event.

Wild card: Farid Basharat

This would be the anti-O'Malley booking. The UFC doesn't love that Basharat has mostly decisions on his record -- so much so that there's been some uncertainty about his security with the promotion. He's ranked in the top 10 by the UFC but in a spot to defend his spot (not attack). This is the kind of athlete who might need to fight down the rankings. Enter Talbott.

Ateba Gautier, middleweight
Who should be next: Loser of Bo Nickal vs. Joe Pyfer on Dec. 12

Hear me out: Gautier's hype train took a major, major hit with the first-round knockout loss to Roman Kopylov. There's no way around it. He took a step up in competition, and fell very flat. In this situation, the UFC can quietly step him back to the prelims somewhere -- or it can create a story. Gautier's stock took a hit but he is still extremely dangerous. There's still intrigue attached to him. Nickal is coming off a strong win at the White House over Kyle Daukaus, but there are still question marks around him. Pyfer is riding high after a finish of Israel Adesanya in his last bout. Whoever loses between Nickal and Pyfer would still be in position for a compelling bout. What's more compelling than this? There is still a way for the UFC to use what's left of the hype around Gautier and make a fight fans will want to watch.

Wild card: Loser of Daukaus vs. Marc-Andre Barriault on Oct. 17

This would be an appropriate next step that would teach us more about Gautier. Kopylov is a legitimate (for lack of a better word) gatekeeper, and Daukaus and Andre Barriault are also proven veterans. Either would challenge Gautier and offer him a chance at redemption.

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.
stories.body:
Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.

It will also be the sixth and final sprint race of the season as Singapore hosts it for the first time.

Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the title championship to 84 points from George Russell.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 17th round of the season.

- Bahrain GP was the worst indictment of F1's new engine regs yet

- Could Malaysia return to F1 calendar? The state of play despite Sepang travel chaos

- Max Verstappen wins disrupted Bahrain GP, Kimi Antonelli extends title lead as George Russell retires

Singapore Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 9

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Sprint Qualifying: 1.30 p.m. - 2.14 p.m.

Saturday, October 10

Sprint: 10 a.m. - 11 a.m.

Qualifying: 2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Sunday, October 11

Singapore Grand Prix: 1 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Singapore Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Marina Bay Street Circuit

Singapore is one of the toughest challenges on the calendar for drivers due to the intense humidity and physically demanding nature of the circuit.

But this time round the drivers will have had a chance to get used to the humid conditions after racing in Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix last weekend.

The Marina Bay Circuit has been on the calendar since 2008 and is one of the standout tracks. The race takes place at night with its breathtaking views of the city's skyline as cars make their way through the tight and twisty circuit.

Drivers can lose around 3kg in body weight after each race due to the amount they sweat.

Singapore Grand Prix

Circuit: Marina Bay Street Circuit; Singapore

Previous winners in Singapore

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2022: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2023: Carlos Sainz (Ferrari)

2024: Lando Norris (McLaren)

2025: George Russell (Mercedes)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2008

Lap record: 1:33.808 Lewis Hamilton (2025)

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel has the most wins with five (2011-2013, 2015 and 2019). From the current grid, Hamilton has four wins (2009, 2014, 2017-2018) and Fernando Alonso with two (2008 and 2010). Pérez (2022), Sainz (2023), Norris (2024) and Russell (2025) have all won a race each here.

Most poles: Vettel (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017) and Hamilton (2009, 2012, 2014, 2018) share the pole record with four each. From the current grid, Charles Leclerc (2019, 2022) has had two pole positions here.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Singapore Grand Prix is set to be thundery showers and light winds throughout the weekend, with highs of 34°C on Friday. The temperature is forecast to drop a degree for the remainder of the weekend.

What happened last time out?
Russell claimed pole position in Singapore last year and crossed the line 0.182 seconds clear of Red Bull's Verstappen, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri behind.

Russell took his second win of the season, but there was plenty of other drama during the race, especially at McLaren.

Norris, who started in fifth, knocked into Piastri when trying to pass him in the first corner. Piastri managed to gain some ground towards the end of the race, but he had to settle for fourth on the day McLaren lifted the trophy for the constructors' title.

Piastri's drivers' championship lead to Norris was separated by only 22 points with six races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

One to watch this weekend is Red Bull and Verstappen after he won the race last weekend. The team brought major upgrades two races ago and improvements to its overall performance has been evident.

Russell, who suffered a major blow to his championship hopes after retiring last time out, will be looking to maximise the points on offer across the weekend.

Mercedes are expected to be strong, while Ferrari are quick in cornering speed. Hamilton has won four times here, so could be a threat. McLaren's Norris and Piastri fell under the radar and struggled for pace in Malaysia.

All will be to play for under the lights in Singapore as we head into the business end of the season.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: USMNT's young stars shine to give Pochettino 'fantastic problem'
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.
stories.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.

The U.S. endured a difficult first half, and scored completely against the run of play in the 28th minute when Hall converted from close range after Mexico keeper Raúl Rangel spilled Gio Reyna's low cross right in front of goal.

- Cavan Sullivan has arrived: U.S. phenom's goal caps a memorable win over Mexico

- Márquez bemoans 'terrible mistakes' as Mexico humbled by USMNT

- USMNT player ratings: Sullivan, Hall 9/10 in big win vs. Mexico

The USMNT began to make more headway in the second half, and doubled its lead in the 62nd minute when Sullivan intercepted a pass from Rangel, and chipped the ball into the net from 35 yards out. The match lost its edge when Mexico's Mateo Chávez was red carded in the 67th minute following a scrap with Sebastian Berhalter.

Malik Tillman finished off the scoring in the 84th minute, latching onto another wayward Mexico pass to firing into the net.

Hall, 18, is just the third USMNT player to score in his first three national team appearances, while 17-year-old Sullivan became the youngest scorer in USMNT history.

"I think it's a fantastic problem for us," Pochettino said about the performances of his team's young players. "I think we will take the right decision in the right moment, but I think it's a very good problem to see.

"Now it's not a moment at all, but yes, we appreciate that situation and of course hope that we will be in that situation that young players perform in the way that they deserve to be with us."

Pochettino also pronounced himself pleased with the way his side weathered Mexico's early pressure.

"I think that this, overall, was a great opportunity to discover ourself, to see ourselves in a difficult game with a very good team. Again, Mexico is a great team," Pochettino said.

"Yes, I think two different maybe halves. The first half I think Mexico started really well. They forced us to play back. We never connected. We were losing all the duels. And then we start to grow after 15, 20 minutes. And I think it was a good lesson the first half because it was the sense of work all together, suffer together even when you are not playing well in the way that you plan to play."

But Pochettino couldn't help but admire the performance of Sullivan, who impressed with his work on both sides the ball.

"I think he's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's a fighter, he's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player with a tremendous quality.

"And then I think Cavan showed in possession with the ball on the field [and] when he need to be chasing people and recover the ball. That is my impression after maybe three weeks together. And that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it's a fantastic news for USA. Hope that continues in that way."

Pochettino was careful to laud Sullivan's young teammates as well, who have largely impressed during this window.

"It's a big moment because we need to be right with them," Pochettino said about the win, and the path forward. "We need to protect them. We need to support them. Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction."

stories.headline: Uncapped NRL trio picked in England's World Cup squad
stories.summary: Ben Talty, Hugo Savala and Max King headline a new-look England squad for the Rugby League World Cup.
stories.body:
Brisbane prop Ben Talty, Canterbury front-rower Max King and Sydney Roosters utility Hugo Savala have been named in England's Rugby League World Cup squad.

Talty and Savala both qualify through ancestry and join Huddersfield-born King in a side assembled by Brian McDermott which contains 10 NRL players.

Savala's Roosters teammate Victor Radley is included along with Newcastle winger Dominic Young and the Dolphins duo of Morgan Knowles and Herbie Farnworth.

Canberra's Perth-bound prop Morgan Smithies has earned selection along with Wests Tigers backrower Kai Pearce-Paul and Gold Coast fullback AJ Brimson, who debuted for England in last year's Ashes whitewash.

McDermott, who is an assistant at the Titans and previously won the Super League title with Leeds, has taken over from Shaun Wane since the 3-0 series defeat.

Leeds halfback Jake Connor -- winner of last year's Man of Steel and controversially left out of the 2025 Ashes -- has again missed the cut, with McDermott preferring Hull KR playmaker Mikey Lewis.

McDermott said: "We have selected the squad after a thorough and deliberate process, underpinned by a unique decentralised preparation model that has allowed us to work closely with the players well before they come together in camp.

"Throughout that process, we have challenged players to develop a deeper understanding of themselves - their strengths, their point of difference, the areas they need to improve and the standards required to perform at international level."

England will kick off against Tonga on October 17 before also facing France and Papua New Guinea in the group stage.
